MEDICAL DECISION MAKING:
Patient presents with chest pain. Patient had saline lock placed and was placed on continuous cardiopulmonary monitoring and pulse oximetry.
I considered high risk diagnoses such as acute myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, pericarditis/myocarditis, pneumothorax, and pneumonia among other diagnoses and I reviewed the ECG for ischemia, arrhythmia, myocardial disease or other
cardiac abnormality.
I independently reviewed the labs and CXR images with CXR showing no evidence of pneumonia, pneumothorax or widened mediastinum
Pulmonary embolism unlikely for the following reasons:
Patient with low pretest probability per Wells or clinical gestalt (<15 percent) and was PERC negative.
Dissection unlikely and no further work-up performed for the following reasons: low probability by history/physical
Pericarditis unlikely as no evidence on history, PE or EKG.
Patient underwent evaluation for ACS. The HEART pathway/score was utilized for risk stratification and found to be less than or equal to 3. Repeat EKG and troponin @ 3 hours were not consistent with acute myocardial infarction/ischemia. Based on this evaluation the patient’s risk of major adverse cardiac events is <1%. Shared decision making occurred with the patient and they will discuss with PMD/Cardiology within 72 hours regarding outpatient management.

item.caption: HS TROPONIN I - Final result (06/01/2025 11:01 PM PDT)

content.content:
High-sensitivity Troponin I (hsTnI) assay can reliably detect low troponin
concentrations relative to conventional troponin assays. It is the preferred
marker of myocardial necrosis as recommended by the Fourth Universal
Definition of Myocardial Infarction Guidelines.
The diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is made based on a rise
or fall of troponin with at least one measurement exceeding the laboratory's
upper limit of normal(indicating myocardial injury), in the context of
reasonable suspicion for coronary ischemia (e.g. typical symptoms, changes
on ECG, evidence for loss of myocardial function or demonstration of
obstructive coronary artery disease).
NOTE: Although abnormal hsTnI values reflect INJURY to myocardial cells, an
elevated hsTnI does not indicate the CAUSE of injury (i.e. ischemia versus
non-ischemic disease).
In some cases, myocardial injury is chronic and relatively stable such that
hsTnI values remain elevated but do not change substantially over hours to
days (examples include chronic kidney disease, heart failure or advanced
patient age).
When determining whether there has been a significant rise or fall of
troponin on serial sampling, absolute change in troponin concentration has
greater diagnostic accuracy for AMI than relative change criteria. A change
of >7 ng/L over a 2-hour interval or a change of >10 ng/L over a 3-hour
interval is suggested as a significant change. If the initial hsTnI is below
or slightly above the 99th percentile upper reference limit, a 50% change
from the baseline is considered significant. If the initial hsTnI is above
the 99th percentile upper reference limit, a 20% change from the baseline
value is considered significant.

item.caption: PRO BNP, BLOOD - Final result (06/01/2025 10:01 PM PDT)

content.content:
The ProBNP test should not be used as absolute
evidence for congestive heart failure (CHF). The
results should be interpreted along with clinical
findings and other laboratory test results. Blood
concentrations of ProBNP may be elevated in patients
who are experiencing a myocardial infarction, in
patients that are candidates for renal dialysis, in
patients that have had renal dialysis, and in one
out of four female patients that are greater than
75 years of age.
